title: Amyloidosis: Tissue Deposition and Congo Red Findings
subject: Pathology
preview: Amyloid represents extracellular deposition of misfolded fibrillar proteins that may damage organs.
quickRevision: Amyloid represents extracellular deposition of misfolded fibrillar proteins that may damage organs.
AL amyloidosis involves immunoglobulin light chains; AA is associated with chronic inflammatory processes.
Cardiac, renal, neural and gastrointestinal involvement can occur depending on amyloid type.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Amyloid represents extracellular deposition of misfolded fibrillar proteins that may damage organs.
Congo red staining shows characteristic apple-green birefringence under polarized light when performed and interpreted correctly.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Typing the amyloid is vital: a positive stain does not identify the specific amyloid protein by itself.
